extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors and news organizations using AP style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and editorial standards from the Associated Press Stylebook blog covering word usage, terminology choices for news events, inclusive reporting, data and AI coverage, and other newsroom style decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Healthcare spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: AP now advises writing 'healthcare' as one word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'healthcare' (one word) according to the AP Stylebook update; this was a considered change announced at ACES.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate entry for Native Americans and Indigenous people/peoples
rubrics_metrics.description: A new, separate entry for Native Americans, Indigenous people/peoples, outside of the race-related coverage entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat terminology for Native Americans and Indigenous people/peoples in their own dedicated entry rather than solely under race-related coverage; follow the specific entry for preferred terms and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated sports terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Updates to sports terms such as 'ping-pong'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt revised entries for sports terms per the Stylebook updates (use the updated preferred forms provided in the Stylebook).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'invasion' for military actions
rubrics_metrics.description: AP is calling Israel's attack on Lebanon an 'invasion' based on observed actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose terms that match the facts: when a military moves thousands of troops across a border and seeks control of territory (and displaced residents cannot return), AP deemed 'invasion' appropriate. Explain what changed and why when adopting such terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Em dash usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when an em dash is appropriate and how to use it; addresses perceptions about em dashes and AI-written text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Em dash is a valid punctuation mark. Use it according to established punctuation rules and AP guidance; do not assume presence of an em dash indicates AI authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to call a conflict a 'war'
rubrics_metrics.description: AP will call the conflict between Israel and Iran a 'war' given scope, intensity and duration of military activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'war' when the scope, intensity and duration of military action on both sides justify the term; other outlets may use 'conflict' or 'fighting'—choose the term that best fits the situation and explain reasoning if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'Persian Gulf' term
rubrics_metrics.description: The AP uses the term 'Persian Gulf' because it is commonly recognized and historically accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the body of water as the 'Persian Gulf' in standard usage; use alternate terms such as 'Arabian Gulf' only in direct quotations or when context requires it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming bodies of water amid political renaming (Gulf of Mexico example)
rubrics_metrics.description: AP will continue to refer to the Gulf of Mexico by its traditional name while acknowledging a U.S. presidential choice to rename it 'Gulf of America'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a name change is ordered by a domestic authority but not widely recognized internationally, AP uses the historically established name while acknowledging the new name chosen by the authority; consider global recognition and authority scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI coverage: avoid anthropomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance advises journalists to avoid language that attributes human characteristics to AI systems or uses gendered pronouns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attribute human feelings, intentions or gendered pronouns to AI systems; remember systems are built by people and reflect human biases and aims. Use precise terminology for AI and generative AI and avoid misleading humanizing language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and terms for AI coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: New entries added on generative artificial intelligence and 10 key AI terms to help journalists explain AI accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Stylebook's AI entries and key terms to accurately define and explain AI concepts in reporting; apply consistent terminology from the Stylebook when covering AI topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: A new chapter emphasizes the importance of inclusive reporting and editing to ensure accuracy and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the inclusive storytelling chapter's guidance to avoid bias and ensure coverage is accurate, fair and respectful; use the chapter immediately available to subscribers for concrete terms and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on suicides
rubrics_metrics.description: AP policy on reporting suicides is 'to not go into detail on the methods used.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid detailed descriptions of suicide methods in reporting; weigh public interest against potential harm and follow the Stylebook's guidance to minimize risk of contagion or harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polling coverage guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere existence of a poll is not enough to make news; poll results that seek to preview the outcome of an election must never be the lead, headline or single subject of any story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize polls, avoid using polls as primary news without broader reporting, and never make previewing-poll results the lead or sole focus; follow the polling chapter for detail on methodology reporting and responsible presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual harassment vs sexual misconduct terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that 'sexual harassment' has a particular legal meaning and that 'harassment' may be too mild for some behavior; guidance on when to use other terms such as 'sexual misconduct'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise terms that reflect the nature and seriousness of the behavior; consult legal definitions and avoid euphemisms that understate severity. When behavior goes beyond legal harassment definitions, consider 'sexual misconduct' or more descriptive language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'Dreamers' term
rubrics_metrics.description: AP policy is to use 'Dreamers' only in direct quotes or with quote marks when explaining the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using 'Dreamers' as an unquoted label in reporting unless directly quoting sources; use quotation marks or explanatory phrasing when introducing the term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on describing 'alt-right' and related movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides clarity around the term 'alt-right' and related terms like 'white nationalism' and 'white supremacism', including definitions and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and describe movements precisely rather than relying on vague labels; explain where terms come from and their associations (e.g., alt-right embraced by some white supremacists/white nationalists). Follow updated entries on spelling and usage for new or coined terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singular 'they' usage
rubrics_metrics.description: New guidance allows limited use of 'they' as a singular pronoun in certain cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use singular 'they' where appropriate per the Stylebook's limited guidance; ensure pronoun agreement and clarity in context and follow the specific examples and restrictions in the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lowercasing 'internet' and 'web'
rubrics_metrics.description: AP decided to lowercase the words 'internet' and 'web' in its 2016 guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lowercase 'internet' and 'web' in prose, following the Stylebook decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respecting subjects' chosen names and pronouns (Manning example)
rubrics_metrics.description: AP will use the name and pronouns requested by the subject (example: Pvt. Chelsea E. Manning and female pronouns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect individuals' stated names and pronouns in coverage; follow the subject's wishes and apply that in headlines and stories as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data journalism practices
rubrics_metrics.description: New data journalism chapter offers guidance on acquiring, evaluating, reproducing and reporting on data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the data journalism chapter for best practices: verify data sources, evaluate methodology, responsibly reproduce and present data, and develop data skills across beats to support accurate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use caution with euphemistic phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance discourages euphemisms (example: 'racially charged') when a stronger term like 'racist' or 'racism' is applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer direct, accurate language rather than euphemisms; if 'racist' or 'racism' applies, use those terms instead of softer phrasing. The Stylebook adds guidance to avoid misleading or evasive language.
